He played [[college football]] for the [[John Carroll Blue Streaks football|John Carroll Blue Streaks]] and signed with the [[St. Louis Rams]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 1998. After four seasons with the Rams, he was a member of the [[Buffalo Bills]] for five seasons and spent his last seven seasons with the [[Washington Redskins]]. He finished his career with 215 consecutive games started, which ties him for seventh all-time along with [[Alan Page]] and [[Ronde Barber]].{{Cite web |last=Yasinskas |first=Pat |date=September 5, 2011 |title=Ronde Barber may move to No. 1 |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nfcsouth/post/_/id/24594/ronde-barber-may-move-to-no-1 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150610231323/http://espn.go.com/blog/nfcsouth/post/_/id/24594/ronde-barber-may-move-to-no-1 |archive-date=June 10, 2015 |access-date=October 28, 2021 |website=ESPN}}{{Cite news |last=Bell |first=Jarrett |date=October 24, 2012 |title=Balance problem puts Redskins LB London Fletcher's streak in doubt |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/2012/10/24/london-fletcher-washington-redskins-linebacker-balance-nfl-streak-in-jeopardy/1655223/ |access-date=October 28, 2012 |work=USAToday.com}} He was inducted into the [[Washington Commanders#Ring of Fame|Washington Commanders Ring of Fame]] in 2019{{Cite web |last=Roscher |first=Liz |date=September 24, 2019 |title=Redskins embarrassingly misspelled London Fletcher's name during Ring of Honor induction |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/redskins-embarrassingly-misspelled-london-fletchers-name-during-ring-of-honor-induction-154657282.html |access-date=December 19, 2025 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en-US}} and joined the team's radio broadcast crew in 2022.{{cite web | last=Selby | first=Zach | title=London Fletcher joins Commanders as in-game analyst | website=Washington Commanders | date=2022-04-28 | url=https://www.commanders.com/news/london-fletcher-joins-commanders-as-in-game-analyst | access-date=2026-03-04}} He currently serves as the [[color commentator]] for the Commanders' radio broadcasts.{{Cite web |title=On-air talent |url=https://www.commanders.com/video/on-air-talent |access-date=December 19, 2025 |website=www.commanders.com |language=en-US}}

'''Logan Lee Mankins''' (born March 10, 1982) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[guard (gridiron football)|guard]] for 11 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL), primarily with the [[New England Patriots]]. After playing [[college football]] for the [[Fresno State Bulldogs football|Fresno State Bulldogs]], he was selected by the Patriots in the first round of the [[2005 NFL draft]]. He spent his final two seasons with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]. Selected to seven [[Pro Bowl]]s and named a first-team [[All-Pro]] twice, Mankins was considered a premier guard in his 11 seasons in NFL, and was also named to the [[National Football League 2010s All-Decade Team|NFL 2010s All-Decade Team]].

Despite his stature as one of the best offensive lineman throughout the Patriots [[Brady–Belichick era|dynasty]], his tenure with the Patriots (2005–2013) coincided with the entire drought between the Patriots first three [[List of Super Bowl champions|Super Bowl]] wins (2001, 2003, 2004) and their last three wins (2014, 2016, 2018). Mankins appeared in two Super Bowls (2007 and 2011), but lost twice.<ref>{{cite magazine | last1=Vrentas | first1=Jenny | last2=Bishop | first2=Greg | title='Gap Years' Patriots on the Brady-Belichick Super Bowl Drought | magazine=Sports Illustrated | date=2021-02-03 | url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2021/02/03/oral-history-patriots-players-during-brady-belichick-super-bowl-gap-drought-daily-cover | access-date=2024-07-24}}</ref>

'''Lionel''' "'''Little Train'''" '''James'''<ref name=posner_02252022/> (May 25, 1962 – February 25, 2022) was an American professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] for the [[San Diego Chargers]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn Tigers]]. Undersized at {{convert|5|ft|6|in|m}} and {{convert|171|lb|kg}},<ref>{{cite web|title=Lionel James|website=NFL.com|url=https://www.nfl.com/players/lionel-james/|access-date=February 25, 2022}}</ref><ref name=wiley_12161985/> he spent his entire five-year NFL career with the Chargers from 1984 to 1988.
